Quantitative measurements from the AgentEval paper: 450 test cases, 3 workflows, 2 model families, Cohen's kappa=0.84, 72% root-cause accuracy, recall 0.89 vs 0.41. Specific and verifiable against the paper.

Specific paper (Huang, Malwe, Wang; arXiv 2601.16280, ICAIBD 2026) with 12 categories spanning tool initialization, parameter handling, execution, and result interpretation; 1,980 test instances across named open-weight and proprietary models; a concrete finding about tool-initialization bottlenecks for smaller models.

Vague: 'domain-specific' is the only taxonomy characterization; no categories, structure, or error types enumerated; n=20 is stated but the taxonomy itself is not described. Insufficient substance for a durable fact.
Specific paper (Zhu et al., arXiv 2606.29955) with named dominant bottlenecks: insufficient spreadsheet inspection and incorrect target-cell selection. Concrete and useful.
Specific paper (Giannouris & Ananiadou; arXiv 2511.22409) with three enumerated error categories: structural, relationship, and semantic/logical errors for LLM-generated UML. Concrete.

Specific paper (Cho et al., arXiv 2605.26731) with six labels, 432-run controlled experiment, and a concrete differential finding: format_violation dominates capable models, wrong_file dominates low-capability models. Durable.
